iOS 27 beta 5 has been released this week, confirming a feature Apple had previously hinted at: a paid upgrade to a higher-tier iCloud+ plan to unlock more Apple Intelligence features.

Upgrading your iCloud+ plan unlocks more iOS 27 AI features

If you already subscribe to iCloud+ or Apple One, upgrading to iOS 27 will bring new features.

You'll gain access to more Apple Intelligence features with usage limits (such as image generation), as well as new HomeKit secure video features for your cameras.

However, according to information in iOS 27 beta 5, the limits on these new features appear to depend on which iCloud+ plan tier you subscribe to.

In the Home app → Home Settings → Apple Intelligence → Cameras & Languages section, iOS 27 now shows how many of your cameras your iCloud+ plan supports for AI summarisation. Quoting a post by Stephen Robles on X:

The right-hand image shared by Robles shows that after tapping "View iCloud+ Plan" on the Cameras & Languages page, a new screen pops up with the following text:

Upgrade your iCloud+ plan to enjoy more Apple Intelligence features. Get more intelligent features, more storage, and more.

The page displays your current plan and offers options to upgrade to a higher tier. The page doesn't list all the different plans yet — this is most likely a minor beta issue that will be fixed before the official release.

Based on what I've seen so far in the beta, the 2TB iCloud+ plan appears to provide AI summarisation for 5 cameras, while the 12TB plan supports up to 15. Details for other plans are not yet clear.

But judging by the wording on this new upgrade page in the beta, it seems almost certain that each higher-tier iCloud+ plan will not only provide AI summarisation for more cameras, but also increase the usage limits for other AI features.

This is consistent with what CEO Tim Cook said during Apple's last earnings call.

What are your thoughts on Apple tying the usage limits of AI features to iCloud+ plans? Feel free to leave a comment and let us know.
